title: Richard Davis, Fosbender and Elgar's violin
summary: Richard Davis studied under Fosbender; Elgar has lost hearing in one ear and describes his violin by a German maker.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Is he a member of this local here?
He's a product of the Civic Symphony. Where? He stood it under Fosbender. That's the first bass player of the regular Chicago Symphony.
So you still play violin, you say, right?
Well, I play a little, not so much now because I've lost the hearing in my right ear. And I can't stand the vibration of these strings now, so I have to practically give up playing.
What kind of violin did you have, by the way? I'm just wondering being a violinist.

Well, I had that violin made by an old man, an old German here whom I met, oh, I guess 25 years ago. Glody. He, he was an old violin maker from Germany. And, and at that time I was doing a lot of teaching and I guess I sold about a half dozen violins which he made. And I still have the same one he made for me. You liked it then? Oh, yes, yes.
